title: Add RAG + agent quickstart template walkthrough (setup, run, observability)
author: Wei Chen
description:
This PR adds a full walkthrough doc for the new RAG + agents quickstart template, aimed at getting a developer from “fresh project” to “running app with traces/metrics visible” with production-minded defaults explained along the way. The page covers: prerequisites + install (CLI + template repo link), required env vars and safe defaults (timeouts/retries/max tokens, tool limits), local run (ingest -> query), how the agent loop uses tool calling and how to debug tool schema failures, and a focused section on observability that helps users interpret spans/metrics and verify their local OTel collector/exporters. It also includes guidance on correlating application logs with Redwood request IDs and a brief note on deployment modes (Hosted vs Dedicated/Private) without over-scoping into infra tutorials.

Notes / scope decisions: We intentionally keep vendor lock-in minimal: the walkthrough describes a “provider abstraction” at a conceptual level and only uses Redwood SDK examples. Telemetry tagging for adoption metrics is described as opt-in and we call out proxy/unknown-header issues and privacy constraints. We do not document eval harness deep-dive here; we link to the evals page and keep this walkthrough focused on first success + operational hooks.

Related: redwood-quickstarts PRs 101–107 (scaffold + OTel + retries + agent loop + docker-compose), observability-pack dashboards PR 156, and docs nav changes in PR 841.
commits: docs(quickstarts): add RAG+agent template walkthrough page
docs(otel): add section on verifying local collector + exporters
docs(troubleshooting): add notes on 401/429/timeouts/tool schema failures
docs: fix broken relative links and align terminology (agent vs workflow)
notable_snippets: Span hierarchy section excerpt: "app.request -> redwood.inference -> rag.retrieve -> agent.loop -> tool.call:<name>" and how to use redwood.request_id to correlate logs/traces.
Metric interpretation excerpt: "redwood.template.tokens_in / tokens_out" and "rag.retrieval.hit" with guidance on avoiding high-cardinality dimensions (no raw user ids, no raw queries).
review_conversation: Elliot Price (2025-03-07): The structure is solid. Two asks: (1) in the first 2–3 paragraphs, define what we mean by “agent” in this template so we don’t imply a Redwood product feature; (2) can you add an explicit “What success looks like” checklist (app runs, streaming works, traces show up, token metrics visible).

Wei Chen (2025-03-07): Done. Added a short definition: “agent loop = orchestrator that can call tools; not a managed Redwood feature”. Also added a success checklist near the top and a “Verify streaming” step using the sample prompt.

Monica Patel (2025-03-08): Please ensure the env var names match the template config schema (REDWOOD_API_KEY / REDWOOD_BASE_URL / REDWOOD_MODEL / OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT). Also, we should mention the default timeout/retry values and where to override them (config file vs env).

Wei Chen (2025-03-08): Updated env var snippet to mirror the template exactly and linked to the config schema section. Added a “Defaults” callout with timeout/retry/backoff + max_tokens and noted how to override via env/config. I also avoided prescribing concurrency defaults since those changed recently.

Allison Grant (2025-03-09): Observability section: please align span names/attributes with the template standard. Specifically: use redwood.request_id, llm.model, llm.operation, and avoid tagging user_id/query as attributes. Also can you call out that tool names are OK but tool arguments must be redacted/sampled (PII).

Wei Chen (2025-03-09): Updated to match the conventions. Removed the example that had query_length as a dimension (kept it as a log field example). Added a redaction note for tool arguments and linked to the redaction rules page.

Christine Wong (2025-03-10): +1 overall. Small resilience note: can we explicitly tell users that streaming reconnect is best-effort and where to look when they see disconnects behind proxies? A short pointer to troubleshooting is fine.

Wei Chen (2025-03-10): Added a short paragraph under “Streaming” explaining disconnect symptoms and linking to troubleshooting (proxies, idle timeouts, retry/backoff). Also clarified that telemetry headers are opt-in due to some proxy restrictions.
Monica Patel (2025-03-11): Approved. Thanks for keeping the defaults explanation tight.
Allison Grant (2025-03-11): Approved (obs alignment looks correct).

Kept Dedicated/Private guidance to a short note + link to deployment options; avoided embedding Docker/K8s recipes here (tracked separately).
